introduction: Every run of the spec, issue, fix and impl tools that reaches the event sink writes its complete event stream to a per-run JSONL file in the state directory. The file is joined to the run's report by a host-independent session_id. --emit-events puts the identical stream on stderr, and tests are isolated from the developer's real state directory.

glossary.envelope: The JSON result document a tool prints on stdout and writes to the report file.
glossary.events file: <state>/events/<tool>-<started_at>-<session_id>.jsonl, holding one JSON event per line for one run.
glossary.human progress: The spinner, step, detail and live-prose lines written to stderr when --emit-events is not set.
glossary.removed flag: --events or --events-file, which are no longer defined.
glossary.session_id: A per-run identifier of 32 lowercase hex characters (16 bytes from crypto/rand). It is the fourth key of every event, a top-level envelope key, and the last part of the report and events file names.
glossary.shell tools: The tools named execute, run_command and powershell in guard.go.
glossary.sink: The component in internal/toolio that stamps each event with the shared header and writes it to the events file and, under --emit-events, to stderr.
glossary.state directory: $XDG_STATE_HOME/agent-fox when XDG_STATE_HOME is non-empty, else $HOME/.local/state/agent-fox. It holds runs/ (reports) and events/ (event streams).
glossary.turn: One model request/response cycle inside a phase, ended by a TurnEndEvent.

requirements.title: Session id
requirements.rationale: A pid repeats across hosts and reboots, so a join key between an events file and its report must come from a source that does not.

criteria.condition: NewRun is called
criteria.action: generate a session_id before any other work, once per run, from 16 bytes read from crypto/rand and hex-encoded to 32 lowercase characters, and expose it on the Run for the sink, the envelope and the file-name functions to read
criteria.contract: Run exposes a session_id string matching ^[0-9a-f]{32}$; NewRun keeps its existing signature

criteria.action: for any two runs created by NewRun, produce session_ids that each match ^[0-9a-f]{32}$ and differ from each other, with no part derived from the pid, the clock or the host

criteria.condition: a run returns before the sink exists, such as a flag-parse failure that still emits an envelope
criteria.action: carry the same session_id in that envelope as the run generated in NewRun
criteria.contract: the usage-error envelope on stdout and in the report file has a 32-hex-character session_id

criteria.action: add no module to go.mod and read randomness only from crypto/rand

requirements.title: Where session_id and the file names appear
requirements.rationale: Each file must name the other so that jq and ls are enough to pair an events file with its report.

criteria.action: stamp every event with a shared header whose keys are, in this order, ts, tool, session_id, type, taking session_id from the run

carry a required top-level session_id string placed immediately after schema_version, identical on stdout and in the report file and present on every envelope including usage-error ones, and describe it in the --schema document
criteria.contract: the stdout envelope, the report file and the --schema output all show session_id; the --schema required list includes it

criteria.action: carry a report_file key that is always present and holds the path the report was written to, or the empty string when it was not written, emitted from the same code that decides the envelope's report_file
criteria.contract: run_end.report_file equals envelope.report_file for every run

criteria.condition: the events file was actually created
criteria.action: append an artifact of kind events_file with a path after the report_file artifact, in stdout, in the report file and under --dry-run, and omit the artifact when the file was not created
criteria.contract: artifacts contains {kind: events_file, path} only when the file exists; the artifact-kind enum in the --schema description includes events_file

criteria.action: name the report <tool>-<started_at>-<session_id>.json through DefaultReportPath, which takes the session id string in place of the pid, and the events file <tool>-<started_at>-<session_id>.jsonl under events/ through the new DefaultEventsPath, both with the same colon-free timestamp and both resolving their base directory through the one stateHome()
criteria.contract: DefaultReportPath and DefaultEventsPath return paths whose stems are identical and whose directories are runs/ and events/ under the same state directory

criteria.condition: stateHome() fails
criteria.action: record the existing report_file_not_written warning at stage report, record events_file_not_written for the events open, and carry on with the run
criteria.contract: the exit code is unchanged and the envelope warnings list contains both codes at stage report

criteria.action: for any run that wrote both files, give the report file name, the events file name and the envelope session_id the same session_id, and make envelope artifacts events_file.path name the events file written and run_end.report_file name the report written

requirements.title: The state directory
requirements.rationale: One state directory, relocatable through the variable the tools already honour, lets tests redirect all writes.

criteria.action: resolve the state directory as $XDG_STATE_HOME/agent-fox when XDG_STATE_HOME is non-empty and as $HOME/.local/state/agent-fox via os.UserHomeDir otherwise, write reports to runs/ and events to events/, create both as needed, and introduce no new environment variable

criteria.condition: XDG_STATE_HOME is set to the empty string
criteria.action: treat it as unset and use $HOME/.local/state/agent-fox

criteria.condition: the caller passes --report-file
criteria.action: change only the report path and keep the events file at its default path under <state>/events/, whose stem is the report's default stem <tool>-<started_at>-<session_id>
criteria.contract: ls <state>/events/*-<session_id>.jsonl finds the events file for a run with an explicit --report-file

requirements.title: The events file is always written
requirements.rationale: A post-mortem record that exists only when someone remembered a flag is missing exactly when it is needed.

criteria.condition: a run reaches the point where openEvents builds the sink
criteria.action: create the events file once with O_CREATE|O_EXCL|O_WRONLY|O_APPEND and mode 0600, never truncating an existing file
criteria.contract: a pre-existing file at the path is left byte-for-byte unchanged and produces the events_file_not_written warning

criteria.action: create the events/ directory with mode 0700, create its parents (agent-fox/ and the state home) with mode 0755, leave an existing events/ directory's mode unchanged, and keep the report modes at 0755 for its directory and 0644 for its file
write each event as one whole-line Write so that a killed process leaves a file made only of complete lines

criteria.condition: a run passes the sink build and then ends through a later usage error, a failing input, a refused preflight, --preflight or --dry-run
criteria.action: leave an events file whose last line is the run_end event
criteria.contract: the final line of the events file parses as JSON with type run_end

criteria.condition: the invocation is -h/--help, --version, --schema, a bare invocation on a terminal, or a usage error refused before the sink is built (a flag-parse failure including a removed flag, an invalid --detail, --total-budget or --input-kind, a bare invocation off-terminal, or an invalid --output)
criteria.action: create no events file and no empty events file, and still write the report as before
criteria.contract: no new file appears under <state>/events/, and the envelope artifacts has no events_file entry

criteria.condition: the events path cannot be resolved or the events file cannot be created (permissions, read-only filesystem, a collision)
criteria.action: record a low warning events_file_not_written at stage report after the sink is attached to the run, register the code in the warning-code list and the code-to-stage table in warncode.go, and neither fail the run nor change its exit code
criteria.contract: the envelope warnings list holds events_file_not_written with severity low and stage report; under --emit-events a warning event for it appears on stderr; the exit code equals that of the same run with a writable state directory

criteria.condition: the events file cannot be created and --emit-events is not set
criteria.action: have no writer and be inactive, and start no heartbeat ticker
criteria.contract: sink.Active() is false and no goroutine ticks; the run output is otherwise unchanged

criteria.condition: the run has an events file
criteria.action: keep running every 15 seconds for the life of the run

requirements.title: --emit-events replaces --events and --events-file
requirements.rationale: Where the stream goes is one boolean decision; the file location is fixed.

criteria.action: accept --emit-events as a shared boolean flag; without it stderr carries the human progress exactly as the default did before this change, and with it stderr carries one JSON event per line and no human line
criteria.contract: Common.EmitEvents is true exactly when the flag is given

criteria.condition: --quiet is set
criteria.action: write nothing to stderr under either value of --emit-events and leave the events file unaffected
criteria.contract: stderr is empty and the events file holds the full stream

criteria.action: remove --events, --events-file, Common.Events, Common.EventsFile, ValidEvents, EventsText, EventsJSONL and the events enum, remove the events and events-file entries from the value-taking-flag table in cmd/fix/main.go, and not add --emit-events to that table

criteria.condition: a caller passes --events-file, as --events-file value or --events-file=value
criteria.action: reject the invocation through the existing flag-not-defined parse-failure path
criteria.contract: exit code 2, stage "usage", message "--events-file was removed; events are always written to <state>/events/" with <state>/events/ as literal text; a report is written and no events file is

criteria.condition: a caller passes --events, as --events value or --events=value
criteria.action: reject the invocation through the existing flag-not-defined parse-failure path
criteria.contract: exit code 2, stage "usage", message "--events was renamed --emit-events"; a report is written and no events file is

criteria.condition: a caller passes both removed flags
criteria.action: name only the first removed flag encountered, because flag parsing stops at the first unknown flag
criteria.contract: the usage-error message contains the text for exactly one of the two removed flags

requirements.title: The stream is complete and independent of the human flags
requirements.rationale: A record filtered by --verbose or --show-text cannot serve as a post-mortem, and Progress must not mistake an always-active sink for JSONL on stderr.

criteria.action: for any run with --emit-events, write to stderr exactly the bytes it writes to the events file
emit a tool_call event for every model tool call and a text event for model prose whether or not --verbose or --show-text is set
record every event field in full, without cutting, abbreviating, dropping for size or sanitising its content
for any combination of --verbose, --show-text and --quiet, produce an events file with the same sequence of event types and field values apart from ts and durations
print the spinner and duration lines unless --emit-events or --quiet is set, deciding this from the explicit --emit-events setting and not from whether the sink is active
criteria.contract: with an active sink and no --emit-events or --quiet, Begin prints; with --emit-events or --quiet it prints nothing and returns a no-op

criteria.condition: Raw is called with prose while --show-text is set and neither --emit-events nor --quiet is
criteria.action: write the prose live to stderr and emit no event, and write nothing and emit no event when --show-text is unset or --emit-events or --quiet is set
criteria.contract: stderr receives the prose bytes in the first case; the sink receives no event from Raw in any case

criteria.action: for any run without --emit-events, write to stderr the same bytes as before this change, apart from the differences caused by the removed flags

requirements.title: text is one event per model turn
requirements.rationale: Per-delta events bloat the file and are not readable; one event per turn carries the whole prose.

criteria.action: carry the keys phase, turn and text after the shared header and no delta key
accumulate the prose of each turn whether or not ShowText is set, join consecutive text blocks of a turn with "\n", and add no trailing newline

criteria.condition: a turn ends with accumulated prose
criteria.action: emit one text event immediately before that turn's turn event, with the same turn number
criteria.contract: in the stream the text event is the line directly before the turn event and both have the same turn value

criteria.condition: a turn ends with no prose
criteria.action: emit no text event for that turn

criteria.condition: a phase ends with prose still buffered and no turn end (cancellation or a stream error)
criteria.action: emit the buffered prose once as a text event before phase_end, with the turn number of the interrupted turn (the last completed turn plus one)
criteria.contract: the text event precedes phase_end, carries turn = completed turns + 1, and the buffer is empty afterwards so the prose is never emitted twice

criteria.action: gain a method for the per-turn text, which Progress implements by emitting the text event

requirements.title: tool_call says what happened
requirements.rationale: A tool_call that records only the tool name cannot explain what the model asked for or how it ended.

criteria.action: carry phase, name and blocked as before and add arguments, ok, exit_code and error, and apply omitempty only to exit_code and error, updating the comment in events.go about omitempty
criteria.contract: arguments and ok are always present; exit_code and error are present only under the rules of 12-REQ-8.4 and 12-REQ-8.5

criteria.condition: a tool call has arguments
criteria.action: record arguments as the JSON the model sent, verbatim apart from insignificant whitespace, and as {} when the model's input is empty
criteria.contract: arguments is valid JSON equal to the model input after whitespace compaction

criteria.condition: the model's tool input is not valid JSON
criteria.action: record arguments as the raw input text encoded as a JSON string, so the event line stays valid and is not dropped
criteria.contract: the line parses as JSON and arguments is a string equal to the raw input

criteria.action: set ok to true when the call's result was not an error result and to false for an error result or a call the shell guard refused, independent of any exit status

criteria.condition: a call to execute, run_command or powershell returns a result from which the exit status can be read
criteria.action: record exit_code, and omit it for a refused call, for a non-shell tool and when the status cannot be read, never guessing or defaulting it to 0
criteria.contract: exit_code is absent from the line in every case except a readable shell exit status

criteria.condition: ok is false
criteria.action: include error holding the text of the error result the call returned, or the guard's message for a refused call, and omit error when ok is true
criteria.contract: error is present exactly when ok is false

criteria.condition: a tool call's result arrives
criteria.action: emit exactly one tool_call event for the call, taking arguments from the ToolCallEndEvent with the same tool-call id and not matching by tool name, with no Verbose() check, and never record the result content
criteria.contract: for two parallel calls to the same tool, each event carries its own call's arguments

criteria.action: take a single struct carrying phase, name, blocked, arguments, ok, exit code and error in place of the former three positional parameters

requirements.title: Tests do not touch the real state directory
requirements.rationale: With the events file always written, every test that reaches App.Main would otherwise write to the developer's real state.

criteria.action: provide one function used from TestMain in internal/toolio, cmd/fix, cmd/impl, cmd/issue and cmd/spec that sets XDG_STATE_HOME to a directory made by os.MkdirTemp, runs m.Run(), removes that directory, and then compares the listing of the real default state directories with a listing taken before the run
criteria.contract: the existing TestMain functions are extended and cmd/impl, cmd/issue and cmd/spec gain one

criteria.action: take the real directories to be $HOME/.local/state/agent-fox resolved with XDG_STATE_HOME ignored, plus the developer's own $XDG_STATE_HOME/agent-fox when it was set before the run

criteria.condition: a file appears under runs/ or events/ of a real directory during the package's test run
criteria.action: fail the package's test run with a message naming the new files
criteria.contract: the test binary exits non-zero and the message lists each new path

criteria.condition: no home directory can be resolved
criteria.action: skip the comparison
criteria.contract: the test run result is decided by the tests alone

criteria.action: keep their own t.Setenv("XDG_STATE_HOME", t.TempDir()) when they assert on a directory's contents, keep HOME pointing at a temp dir in tests that deliberately unset XDG_STATE_HOME (TestTS06_7), and let tests that start a built binary inherit the isolated environment

requirements.title: Interface version, existing tests and documentation
requirements.rationale: Removing text.delta and two flags is a major change under PRD 03, and the steering file requires docs to change in the same change.

criteria.action: set SchemaVersion to 3.0.0 and regenerate and review each cmd/*/testdata/schema.golden.json so that it lists --emit-events and neither --events nor --events-file, the envelope session_id property, and events_file in the artifact-kind enum
criteria.contract: the --schema output of each tool equals its golden file

criteria.action: replace the --events and --events-file Shared flags rows with an --emit-events row, state the new default report file name in the --report-file row, update the Machine-readable progress section (header with session_id, run_end.report_file, tool_call, text, removal of the --verbose and --show-text gates, the usage-error paragraph and the worked example) and the --schema paragraph, add events_file_not_written to the warnings table and events_file to the artifact kinds, and add a 3.0.0 entry to the schema-version changelog

rename the "Report files" section to "State directory" covering runs/ and events/, the new file names, the 0700 and 0600 modes, and an XDG_STATE_HOME row stating that tests set it, and update the heading assertion in docs_test.go (TS-06-63) with it
name --emit-events or the events file, and not --events jsonl or --events-file, as the way to watch spend

use the new behaviour in every test that used the removed flags, the pid file name, the delta field, the --verbose gating of tool_call or the sink-only-when-requested behaviour, in internal/toolio, internal/agentrun/hooks_test.go, cmd/fix/preflight_detail_test.go, docs_events_test.go and docs_test.go, and make the byte-comparison normalisation of TS-06-13 drop session_id as well
criteria.contract: make test passes with no reference to --events, --events-file, text.delta or the pid-based report name outside tests of the removed-flag errors

execution_paths.title: A default run writes an events file and a report that name each other

steps.action: runs a tool such as `impl` with no events flag and XDG_STATE_HOME pointing at a state directory
generates a 32-hex-character session_id in NewRun
creates <state>/events/<tool>-<started_at>-<session_id>.jsonl exclusively with mode 0600 inside an events/ directory of mode 0700, and starts the heartbeat
writes every event with the header ts, tool, session_id, type, one whole line per event, ending with run_end carrying report_file
writes <state>/runs/<tool>-<started_at>-<session_id>.json and prints the envelope with session_id and an events_file artifact
pairs the two files with ls and jq through the shared session_id

execution_paths.title: --emit-events streams the complete model activity to stderr and the file

steps.action: runs a model-backed tool with --emit-events and without --verbose or --show-text
accumulates a turn's prose and matches each ToolCallEndEvent to its ToolResultEvent by tool-call id
emits one tool_call event per call with arguments, ok and, when readable, exit_code, then one text event immediately before the turn event
writes each event line to stderr and to the events file, with no human progress line
finds the stderr bytes identical to the events file content

execution_paths.title: A caller passes a removed flag

steps.action: runs a tool with --events-file out.jsonl or --events jsonl
fails with flag provided but not defined
rewrites the failure into the removal or rename message
writes a usage-error envelope with session_id and a report file, exits 2, and creates no events file

execution_paths.title: The events file cannot be created and the run carries on

steps.action: runs a tool with --emit-events while <state>/events cannot be written
fails to create the events file and leaves the sink with stderr as its only writer
records the low warning events_file_not_written at stage report after the sink is attached
emits the warning as an event on stderr
finishes with the unchanged exit code and an envelope without an events_file artifact

execution_paths.title: A package test run leaves the real state directory untouched

steps.action: runs make test
lists the real state directories, sets XDG_STATE_HOME to a MkdirTemp directory and calls m.Run()
call App.Main, which writes reports and events files into the temporary directory
removes the temporary directory and compares the real listing with the earlier one, failing the package with the new file names if they differ

execution_paths.title: A default run without --emit-events keeps the human progress

steps.action: runs a model-backed tool with --show-text and no --emit-events on a terminal
decides stderr behaviour from --emit-events and --quiet and not from the always-active sink
prints the spinner and duration lines and streams the model prose live through Raw without emitting an event from it
records the same run's complete event stream in the events file

symbols.name: ToolCallEndEvent
symbols.notes: phase.go reads Block.Name and string(Block.Input). Source not readable; signature taken from call sites.

symbols.name: ToolUseBlock
symbols.signature: type ToolUseBlock struct { ID string; Name string; Input []byte-or-string }
symbols.notes: The ID field is assumed and not used in the repo; R8 needs it to pair a result with its call. Use whatever the SDK provides if it is named differently.

symbols.name: ToolResultEvent
symbols.notes: Message has ToolName, IsError, Content (Content.Text()); ToolCallID is assumed.

symbols.name: ToolExecutionEndEvent
symbols.signature: type ToolExecutionEndEvent struct { Name string; IsError bool; ElapsedMS int64 }
symbols.notes: Whether it or the result carries a shell exit status is not known.

symbols.name: TextDeltaEvent
symbols.notes: Also core.TextEndEvent and core.TurnEndEvent{Usage}; a turn's text events are assumed to precede its TurnEndEvent.
